doc.title: Stefon Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2020

title: Bobby Hutcherson's tune 'Now'
summary: Rowe thanks Harris for recording Hutcherson's 'Now'; Harris says it is a platform for many voices and unites the ensemble.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. Speaking of Bobby Hutcherson, I wanted to make sure I thanked you — last night I was checking out some of your recordings and I said, I was sitting in my kitchen and I went, “Oh my God.” And my wife goes, “What’s the matter?” And I said, “Well Stefon did Bobby Hutcherson’s song called ‘Now.’” And I don’t want to spend a lot of time on that but that song used to fascinate me. It was so beautiful. And so thank you for doing a version of it.

Yeah. What a fantastic piece of music, and it functions in the exact way that you hope that any great piece of music will function in that it becomes this phenomenal platform for the expression of a myriad of voices. It’s a so beautiful melody that it’s repeated with an absolutely perfect harmony under it. But it just sort of breathes and it allows you to step into the middle of the song and sing your truth in your own way. It’s a rare thing to come across a composition like that. And unfortunately that’s not a piece that’s very well known, but I think hopefully the Blackout recording will help. I think Bill Watrous did a recording of it and one or two other people are starting to do that too. It’s definitely one of my favorites for the band to play because, because of the repeated melody it’s not so much about one soloist at a time. It’s really about us coming together under this repeated melody, how we continually change the texture around it. So playing that piece of music helps unite us as an ensemble and keeps us focused on our purpose.
